newsitem.title: USA: FAA proposes new inspection regime for Boeing 727s.
newsitem.headline: FAA proposes new inspection regime for Boeing 727s.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration has proposed a new airworthiness directive to ensure the structural integrity of older Boeing 727 aircraft.

The proposal, published in the Federal Register Thursday, would require additional, expanded inspections and repair of cracked structures. It would also apply to more planes than the existing directive.
The new directive would incorporate a National Transportation Safety Board recommendation for additional inspections to detect cracks in the fuselage skin structure.
It also makes changes in inspections to account for modifications to planes that may increase or change load distributions, including conversions to all-cargo configurations.
There would be inspection thresholds for all Boeing 727 series aircraft and revisions to ensure inspection programs are carried out on schedule, even when ownership or operators change.
The FAA said its proposal would take about 1,200 work hours per plane at a cost of about $72,000 for each of the 74 affected aircraft registered in the United States.
It would consider any comments received by July 7.
